overview: Memeware 7.3's Step is a two-mode module. Vanilla simply raises the client's stepHeight to the Height setting (1-10 blocks) so the local physics climb walls the server never granted. NCP mode hooks the ClimbSlabEvent to combine a 1.0 stepHeight with staged C04 packets: while the Speed module is off the pre-phase grants a vanilla-compatible step height of 1.0, and once the bounding box has actually risen more than 0.6 (up to 1.0) the module injects two C04Position packets at +0.42 and +0.75 with onGround false - splitting the climb into sub-threshold vertical moves - then runs the client timer at 0.4 for exactly two ticks so the reported positions converge.

sections.p: The module is three handlers and two fields (timerSlow, height). The first UpdateEvent consumer is the stepHeight setter: in Vanilla mode it assigns mc.thePlayer.stepHeight = height (the setting, 1-10), in NCP mode it holds stepHeight at the vanilla 0.6. The ClimbSlabEvent consumer is the NCP-mode packet injector. The second UpdateEvent consumer is the timer countdown: it decrements timerSlow every tick and restores timerSpeed to 1.0 when the counter reaches zero, giving the 0.4 timer a lifetime of exactly two ticks. onDisable resets stepHeight to 0.6 regardless of mode, so a disabled module never leaves the client able to climb.

Vanilla mode is a one-line client-side abuse: stepHeight = height. The setting accepts 1 to 10, so a player can climb a full block (or more) in a single tick with no packet of its own - the server only ever sees the resulting movement packets. The mode does nothing to hide those moves: it does not stage the climb, does not adjust the timer, and does not touch the onGround flag, so the server sees an instantaneous 1-block vertical rise while the player is grounded on both sides of it.

The NCP mode splits the step into two phases. In the ClimbSlabEvent pre phase, if the Speed module is not toggled, the event's step height is set to 1.0 - the client physics are allowed to climb a full block, and because the event fires for genuine block contact this reads as a vanilla-compatible step. In the post phase (or with Speed on), the module measures the actual climb from the bounding box (getEntityBoundingBox().minY - posY) and, only when it exceeds 0.6 and stays within 1.0, sends two C04PacketPlayerPosition packets at posY + 0.42 and posY + 0.75 with onGround false, then sets timerSpeed to 0.4 and arms timerSlow = 2. The two offsets split a 0.6-1.0 climb into a 0.42 plus a 0.33 vertical move, each below the per-move step thresholds of server-side models, and the two ticks of 0.4-speed playback stretch the client's subsequent movement so the reported positions catch up to the climb without an obvious spike. When the step is outside the 0.6-1.0 window the module still arms timerSlow but sends nothing.

files.label: Step.java (module)
files.explanation: The whole module is this 70-line file. The first UpdateEvent handler sets stepHeight per mode: the Height setting (1-10) in Vanilla, the vanilla 0.6 in NCP mode. The ClimbSlabEvent handler is the NCP-mode injector: in the pre phase it grants a 1.0 step height only when the Speed module is off (so the client can actually climb), and in the post phase it measures the bounding-box rise and, for climbs between 0.6 and 1.0, sends the two C04 packets at +0.42 and +0.75 with onGround false and drops the timer to 0.4 for two ticks via timerSlow. The second UpdateEvent handler decrements timerSlow and restores timerSpeed to 1.0 when it reaches zero, so the slow playback lasts exactly two ticks after each step. onDisable restores stepHeight 0.6. The module never sends a C03 with a modified onGround flag and never touches the movement delta - all of its evasion is the C04 pair and the timer burn.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (step envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's vertical allowance in vDistRel grants the step envelope only through isStepUpByNCPDefinition: a move qualifies as a step when both endpoints are grounded per NCP's own block ray trace (not the packet flag) and the y-distance is at most the configured sfStepHeight (0.6 by default for 1.8 players on pre-1.20.5 servers), or when NCP's collide-based couldStepUp simulation reproduces the climb. The module's injected C04s claim onGround false, so they cannot enter the envelope at all - the +0.42 move is only forgiven when a real jump was registered in the previous move, and a step-up is not a jump. When the two packets are folded into the tick's merged move, the ground-to-ground climb of 0.75-1.0 exceeds sfStepHeight 0.6, the step envelope fails, and vDistRel measures the rise against the gravity/momentum model: yDistanceAboveLimit lands near the full climb height and the (max(hdist,0) + max(ydist,0)) * 100 violation fires with a set-back. The two ticks of 0.4 timer only slow the client; they do not change what the merged move contains.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation: MorePackets counts every serverbound move packet into morePacketsFreq (an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets) and scores the window against cc.morePacketsEPSMax (22/s, 20 ideal) with a burst path on the newest half-second bucket (15 packets, 10 direct-violation). Each NCP-mode step fires two extra C04 packets in the same tick as the regular move, tripling that tick's packet count. On flat ground the baseline 20/s leaves headroom, but ascending stairs or a sequence of 1-block climbs (one step every one or two ticks) turns the sustained rate into 40-60 packets per second, blowing through the 22/s window and tripping the burst path on the first concentrated climb. Because the check is content-blind, the staged offsets provide no cover - the count is the count, and the module's 0.4 timer burn does not reduce the number of packets sent per climb.

countering.label: Step (grounded vertical bound)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Step check only examines moves where the client and Hawk both consider the player on the ground and Hawk's own step test says the move is not a step; it then flags any dY above 0.6 or below -0.0784 with punishAndTryRubberband. Hawk's testStep (MoveEvent line 320) rejects a candidate step as soon as the climbed block top is more than 0.6 above the previous Y, so a 0.75-1.0 climb is never a step for Hawk. The module's intermediate C04s escape the guard because they claim onGround false (the check returns early when the client does not claim ground), but the C03 that carries the player's real position - the one-tick 0.75-1.0 rise from ground to ground - has both sides grounded, is not a step, and exceeds the 0.6 bound, so the check fires and rubber-bands the player to the server position. The vanilla-height stepHeight abuse (Height 1-10) fails the same way: any rise above 0.6 with both sides grounded and no accepted step is a violation.
